title: MindFort Partners with MorphLLM | MindFort Blog
summary: MindFort is partnering with MorphLLM to bring abliterated open models to MindFort Swarms, with inference built to run large-scale security agent swarms.
body_markdown:
We're excited to announce a new partnership with the team at[MorphLLM ↗](https://www.morphllm.com/) . Together, we're bringing the latest abliterated open models to MindFort Swarms.


## Why did we partner with Morph?


Agent-led cyberattacks are rising fast. The attacking agents probe targets around the clock and never get tired. Defenders need to be equipped with the same capabilities now.


Defending against that takes swarms of agents testing your systems in parallel, so we needed a partner that could meet the inference requirements of swarms at that scale. The team at Morph has built inference for exactly this use case. They also host the latest models for cyber, which made them a natural fit.


## What does this mean for MindFort customers?


MindFort Swarms will be powered by the latest cyber-capable models. That includes abliterated open models that take on authorized offensive work without refusing. Morph serves these models at the scale a large swarm needs. As new models ship, Swarms can put them to work.


MindFort is designed to let teams safely deploy security swarms. Those swarms quickly find vulnerabilities in your products and services. You keep the same scoping, rate limits, and validated findings you use today. To see Swarms run against your own app,[book a demo ↗](https://cal.com/team/mindfort/platform-demo) .


## FAQ


### Who is MindFort partnering with?


MindFort is partnering with MorphLLM. Morph builds inference designed for AI agents. The partnership brings the latest abliterated open models to MindFort Swarms.


### What is an abliterated model?


An abliterated model is an open-weight model with its refusal behavior removed. It completes authorized offensive security tasks that a stock model might decline.


### Why does MindFort need a dedicated inference partner?


Agent swarms run many agents in parallel over long engagements. That takes high throughput and long context at a sustainable cost. Morph's inference is built for that workload.
